steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Campaigns aim to achieve specific changes in policy, behaviour, or awareness. Successful campaigns have clear messages, identifiable targets, and measurable goals. | Key Fact: Campaign methods include: petitions, marches and demonstrations, social media campaigns, lobbying elected representatives, public meetings, letter-writing, boycotts, and civil disobedience. | Key Fact: Advocacy means representing and arguing for the rights and interests of others, especially those who may not be able to represent themselves effectively. | Key Fact: Grassroots campaigns are built from the community level up (e.g. local residents opposing a development). Top-down campaigns are led by established organisations (e.g. Oxfam, Amnesty International).
